findings.message: tickDates takes the newest commit whose diff has a `+- [x] \`Tn\`` line as the date the task was ticked. Ticking a box is not the only thing that produces that line. A commit that rewords an already-ticked task's title, reorders the task list, reformats or rewrites the file (for example a CRLF→LF normalisation), or moves it to archive/ with edits large enough that git treats it as a fresh add also re-emits `+- [x] \`Tn\``, and the task then gets that later date. Since the scan runs newest first, that later commit wins. Fix: count a commit as the tick only when the same diff also removes that task as `-- [ ] \`Tn\``, or when the task's `[x]` state actually changes between that commit and its parent. Add test rows for a title edit and a whole-file rewrite.
findings.scenario: T1 ticked 2026-10-03, then its title reworded on 2026-10-09 → T1.doneAt = 2026-10-09. writeTasks overwrites done_at on the next sync (done_by is null), and the history shows 'T1 … done' on Oct 9.

findings.message: `repoPhases: r.phaseTimes ?? {}` goes into meta, and upsertSpecProposal writes `meta = excluded.meta`. A push from an older plugin has no phaseTimes, so SpecRecordInput defaults it to `{}`. The fingerprint then differs from the stored meta, the sync writes, and every stored repo phase is erased. This contradicts the push.ts comment, which says an older plugin's push leaves amax's stored dates alone; that only holds for createdAt, which is coalesced. Fix: when phaseTimes is absent, keep the stored `meta.repoPhases`, the same way prior.pr and prior.verdict are kept. Treat absent as unknown rather than empty, so the fingerprint doesn't see a change.
findings.scenario: CI with the new plugin stores repoPhases {proposal, verify} for FLT-301. Then a developer's older plugin pushes the default branch → meta.repoPhases = {} → the 'Approved/Verified in the repo' history lines disappear, and pins on repo:verify resolve to null.

findings.message: `shippedToProd` is a new hand-written copy of the In Prod rule. The same `exists (select 1 from delivery.deployment d where d.release_id = p.release_id and d.released and d.voided_at is null)` is already written out at queries.ts:66 (`in_prod`, which the list and CSV use since 093), and in services.ts:39/466. The chart and the 'Released this month' count can now drift from the card's 'In Prod' label. Fix: define the rule once, export it, and have line 66 and both new uses (shippedPerWeek, phaseCounts) use it.
findings.scenario: A later change makes In Prod also require `d.status = 'deployed'` and edits only line 66 → a proposal whose card shows 'Released · from repo' is still counted in 'Shipped to Prod per week'.

findings.message: Repo phase history lines set `by` to the literal source string ("specclaw") instead of a person or an agent acting for one, unlike every other history line, which goes through who(). Show who the repo names (the proposal's owner or the change author, resolved the way the sync resolves it) or 'from the repo', so the 'who did it' column stays meaningful.
findings.scenario: The proposal page's history shows 'Verified in the repo · specclaw' instead of a person.

findings.message: The mock's history disagrees with the code. It shows 'Proposed in the repo' and 'Verified in the repo · PR #12 raised' on one line. REPO_PHASE produces no 'Proposed' line (state.json's proposal phase reads as 'Approved'), and 'PR raised' is its own line. Bring the mock in line with the implementation and the README (Approved / Tasks planned / Verified / PR raised / Archived).

createdOf decides whether the header's `**Created:**` day matches state.json's proposal time by comparing it to the UTC ISO string. The header day is the author's local day, so a proposal made on the same local day, but on another UTC day, falls back to midnight UTC and loses its real time. Either document that the header day is UTC, or compare it within a day's tolerance.
findings.scenario: Created: 2026-10-01, written in Sri Lanka at 2026-10-01 03:00 +05:30 (state.json at 2026-09-30T21:30Z) → createdAt = 2026-10-01T00:00Z instead of 2026-09-30T21:30Z.

findings.message: The new repo dates have no future bound. `createdAt` (SyncInput, SpecRecordInput), `TaskInput.doneAt` and `phaseTimes` accept any datetime and are written straight into `delivery.proposal.created_at`, `delivery.task.done_at` and `meta.repoPhases`. `PushInput.committedAt` is held to `SKEW_MS`, and this repo already raised a finding when a sync date (`committedAt` on SyncInput and markSynced) shipped without that bound. This change repeats the same defect for three new fields. Fix: run every repo date through the push's skew rule (one shared refinement): refuse a date past now + SKEW_MS or treat it as unknown, in both schemas and in `sync_proposal`'s TaskInput.
findings.scenario: A change.md header with the typo `**Created:** 2062-10-17`, or a commit made on a machine whose clock runs a year ahead → the proposal's created_at is 2062 and the task's done_at is a year in the future. The history sorts those lines above everything else, and any created-at or done-at window miscounts them.

findings.message: `phaseTimes` defaults to `{}` when an older plugin leaves it out, and `desired()` then writes `meta.repoPhases: {}`. So 'the plugin didn't send it' reads the same as 'the repo has no phases' and wipes the stored phases. The comment says amax keeps what it has, and `createdAt` and `doneAt` do that through coalesce and case, but `repoPhases` doesn't. Because `repoPhases` is part of the fingerprint, a newer CI push and an older local plugin keep rewriting the row back and forth, each time with an audit row. A pinned `repo:verify` line then resolves to null (gone). Fix: make it `.optional()` with no default, and carry the stored `meta.repoPhases` over when it's absent, the same way pr and verdict are kept from main.
findings.scenario: CI with the new plugin pushes CON-031 and repoPhases gets {proposal, verify}. A developer's 093-era plugin then pushes the same commit → meta.repoPhases = {}, the history loses 'Approved/Verified in the repo', and a pin on repo:verify returns null. The next CI push writes them back, so each alternation is an update plus an audit row.

findings.message: A sync can now rewrite `created_at` and task `done_at`, and `repoDatesStale` forces a write when the only difference is a date. The audit's before and after don't record those dates, so a date-only correction leaves an audit row whose before and after look identical. Add createdAt, and the task dates the write changed, to before and after.
findings.scenario: The second push in the AC-1 test changes created_at from Nov 10 to Oct 1 → the audit row shows the same phase, title, tasksDone and owner on both sides, with nothing showing what changed.

findings.message: `tickDates` runs inside the same try as the author read. If the `git log -p` walk fails (for example maxBuffer on a long history), the catch drops the author that was already read and returns `author: undefined`. A failure to read tick dates then shows up as an owner amax couldn't read, so a real owner change doesn't apply. Catch tick-date failures separately and leave only `doneAt` unset.
findings.scenario: A change with a very long change.md history goes past 64 MB of patch output → the record goes out with author undefined, so an Owner change made in the repo is never applied.
